authorization: etymologise remaining Indo-Aryan surveys. do not rebuild. work autonomously and do what you can, you have 8 hours, i will review once your time is done.

proposals.evidence: Full mudrā lists Prakrit muddiā, Punjabi mundī “ring”, Gujarati mū̃drī, Marathi mudī and Oriya mudi. The selected western/eastern survey mundī/muḍī/mundrī forms preserve that ring family, including source aspiration and optional nasal or r. The ancient head is itself probably an Iranian loan according to Turner; the modern link identifies its later Indo-Aryan continuations and does not erase that qualification. Extra diminutive material and potentially maṇḍala-derived forms are excluded.

proposals.evidence: Turner explicitly includes Oriya pilā “small; child” under *pilla, with Prakrit pella/pīlua and Bengali pil/children expressions. These adjacent eastern boy forms fit that full child word. The entry derives the older family from Dravidian; this reflex link concerns its later Indo-Aryan continuation, with Oriya-mediated regional transmission left open.
